parts.visual:
A paradox of innovation: Sometimes, to build the future, you must destroy your own profitable past.

The Concept:
1. Cannibalization: When a company releases a new product that is so good, it destroys the sales of its own older, highly profitable product.
2. The Executive Dilemma: Why spend millions developing a product that will just steal your own customers?
parts.audio: Product Cannibalization is when your new product destroys the sales of your old product. Executives must choose to cannibalize themselves, or wait for a competitor to do it to them.

questions.question: Your company makes $1 Billion a year selling MP3 players. Your engineers invent a new smartphone that plays music, meaning nobody will ever buy your MP3 player again. What do you do?
options: Hide the smartphone technology in a vault.
Launch the smartphone immediately. It is better to cannibalize your own sales than to let a competitor cannibalize them for you.
Only sell the smartphone in other countries.
questions.correct_answer: Launch the smartphone immediately. It is better to cannibalize your own sales than to let a competitor cannibalize them for you.
questions.explanation: This was the exact dilemma Apple faced with the iPod and the iPhone. Steve Jobs chose to kill the iPod to birth the iPhone.

questions.question: Listen to the defensive executive. What mistake is he making?
questions.tts_text: We cannot launch streaming video. It will destroy our DVD sales, and DVD sales make up 80% of our revenue! We must protect our core business.
options: Protecting the past at the expense of the future (The Innovator's Dilemma).
questions.correct_answer: Protecting the past at the expense of the future (The Innovator's Dilemma).
questions.explanation: This is why Blockbuster died and Netflix lived. Blockbuster refused to cannibalize their DVD late-fees.

questions.question: Why is 'Cannibalization' so difficult for public companies to execute?
options: Because Wall Street analysts demand quarterly profit growth. If a new product temporarily kills profits while replacing an old product, the stock will crash and the CEO might be fired.
questions.correct_answer: Because Wall Street analysts demand quarterly profit growth. If a new product temporarily kills profits while replacing an old product, the stock will crash and the CEO might be fired.
questions.explanation: It takes immense executive courage to sacrifice short-term profits for long-term survival.

questions.question: What is 'Planned Obsolescence'?
options: Designing a product with a limited useful lifespan so it will become obsolete (unfashionable or no longer functional) after a certain period of time, forcing the customer to buy the newer version.
questions.correct_answer: Designing a product with a limited useful lifespan so it will become obsolete (unfashionable or no longer functional) after a certain period of time, forcing the customer to buy the newer version.
questions.explanation: This is the dark side of cannibalization—forcing the consumer to upgrade by artificial means.

pairs.match: A reduction in sales volume or market share of one product as a result of the introduction of a new product by the same producer
Designing a product with an artificially limited useful life
Innovation that creates a new market and value network, eventually displacing established firms
The primary area or activity that a company was founded on or focuses on
